## General Summary

The document set outlines the ethical and administrative requirements for a proposed study titled **“EcoLegis: Legislative Document Management & AI Summary System”** at Bulacan Polytechnic College. It includes English and Filipino informed-consent forms and a formal request to conduct research among students and Guidance Office personnel. The study aims to assess the proposed system’s functionality, usability, usefulness, and effectiveness. The forms emphasize informed participation, confidentiality, anonymity, privacy, voluntary withdrawal, and the absence of foreseeable risks. Researchers also seek approval from the College Office of the Vice President for Planning, Research and Extension before proceeding.

## Page Range Breakdown

### Pages 1-2 — Informed Consent Forms

Pages 1 and 2 present equivalent informed-consent forms in English and Filipino, respectively. The forms explain the study’s nature and purpose, why participants were selected, potential benefits and risks, and their rights to ask questions, skip questions, and withdraw without explanation. Participants are assured that their answers and identities will remain confidential and anonymous. They are also informed that interviews may be recorded and that they may receive a transcript for review, correction, or expansion. Participants may later be asked to validate study results and suggest improvements. Both forms require the respondent’s printed name and signature and state that the Office of the Vice President for Research and Extension must sign or approve them before the study begins. Some participant-specific information is illegible in the extracted text.

### Page 3 — Request for Permission to Conduct Research

This page contains a letter dated **September 25, 2026**, addressed to **Mrs. Ma. Jessica R. Quiambao**, a Guidance Office counselor at Bulacan Polytechnic College. Fourth-year Bachelor of Science in Information Systems students request permission to conduct the **EcoLegis** study with students enrolled during A.Y. 2026-2027 and with Guidance Office personnel. Student testing is proposed during vacant class periods.

The researchers promise written or verbal consent, confidentiality, anonymity, privacy in published data, freedom to withdraw without penalty, and no foreseeable risks or advantages or disadvantages from participation. All research data will be preserved anonymously for reuse by other researchers. The letter concludes with signatures from the student researchers and notation by the research adviser and the Office of the Vice President for Research and Extension.
